Food! I 've had to rehab the way I think about cooking to be frugal so we can live off of one income and I can be a stay at home mom. Here are some of my obvious/not so obvious tips:

You can save so much money just by cooking your favorite dish at home. You can google about every restaurant favorite and someone has figured out a way to make it. I've stopped going to Starbucks completely now as every drink you can make from your pantry as long as you have ice, a pitcher of cold coffee, access to make fresh hot coffee, and your favorite flavoring (Carmel for me). Starbucks Recipes: http://billcutterz.com/blog/2014/06/starbucks-coffee-recipes/

Baked Goods: I never buy premade baked goods like cookies, brownies, and cakes from grocery store bakeries anymore (I will buy them from specialty bakeries though for special occasions). Check your grocery circulars - I bought brownie mix for 69 cents a box last week. You can go a step further and skip the box to just mix your own from raw pantry ingredients: Brownies:http://baking.food.com/recipe/fudgy-brownies-from-scratch-382771

Italian Cuisine: my husband is Italian American and makes better pasta dishes than any restaurant. A few quick tips: If you are making a tomato based sauce cook up some diced onion first, it makes it sweeter, add a splash of red wine to bolden the flavor. You can make the cheapest can of Prego taste gourmet with this trick. Alternatively, you can take a 1/2 day and cook up a big batch of sauce yourself and freeze it. Major savings.

Sides: Don't buy Rice a Roni, its such a waste! It takes twice as long to cook than regular rice and twice as expensive. Buy a 5lb bag of rice and google flavor recipes. Here are my go-to's: http://www.thescramble.com/cooking-basics/ways-to-liven-up-plain-steamed-rice/

Soup: Never buy canned chicken soup again. Make your own stock from rotisserie chicken carcuss and freeze it. When you want to make soup toss it in a pan and warm it up. Mix in some fresh seasoning, rice/pasta/or egg noodles, and some pieces of chicken. Done in ten minutes and taste SO MUCH better than any can.

Veggies: Why would you buy frozen? It is not as cheap as you think and they taste NASTY. Go to international markets and pick up veggies. Blanch them and freeze them yourself. It takes 15 minutes of prep for 1/2 the price and tastes so much better. Then you can take them out of the freezer and still cook them any way you want

Costco! You don't need to be a member to shop if you get a gift card. Find someone who will put money on a Costco gift card for you and are you gold! Then go buy the $20 package of hamburger meat. When you get home break it up into 1/2lbs ziplock bags and freeze. You will have hamburger for a month at 1/2 the price of a regular supermarket.

Coupon guys! Seriously, do you know that this week VONS put out a $5 off $50 or more? That is free money. Even if you are a single dude living off of hot dogs and beer you are still going to spend $50. Cut that shit out and use it. No shame! Use the card saving apps too. If you are loyal to specific items you will get them a discounted prices. We get DeChecco pasta for $1.75 a box now. It's on the shelf price is around $3.50.
